title: Lance Stroll to race in F1 Australian Grand Prix despite failing to set qualifying lap time
content:
MELBOURNE, Australia — Lance Stroll will be allowed to race in the Australian Grand Prix despite failing to set a lap time within 107 percent of the fastest Q1 time.

The safety regulation has been around the sport on and off since it was first introduced in 1996 (it was dropped between 2002 and 2011). It applies to qualifying, as a way to avoid speed disparities and ensure safety.

Essentially, a driver needs to record a lap time within 107 percent of the fastest Q1 lap to be able to compete in the grand prix, and that number is determined when you multiply the fastest time (in seconds) by 1.07.

Stroll failed to set a qualifying lap time, and Aston Martin needed to request for the stewards to allow him to start Sunday’s Formula 1 race. The regulations allow the stewards to take other circumstances, like satisfactory lap times, into consideration.

While a majority of the time, this is an open-and-closed type of scenario because of how strong the strong F1 era has been, that’s not exactly the case for Aston Martin.

The Silverstone-based team has been plagued with issues since Bahrain preseason testing.

Team principal Adrian Newey went as far as saying Thursday that they may run limited laps on Sunday’s race given vibration issues, and on Friday, he revealed the team has a battery shortage, with the only two available currently being used in each car. And when it came to Stroll’s lap times in practice, he was off the mark in first and second practice.

The stewards laid out their reasoning for allowing Stroll to participate in Sunday’s race, which included his F1 experience and how many kilometers he’s driven in the car so far this year as well as Fernando Alonso’s performance. The Spaniard qualified 17th. Additionally, Aston Martin decided not to allow Stroll to compete “in qualifying due to a damaged oil line in the car, out of prudence, to enable them to undertake further investigations.”

This came after Stroll didn’t run in third practice earlier Saturday, because of a suspected internal combustion engine issue.

Max Verstappen and Carlos Sainz are also allowed to participate in the grand prix, despite failing to set lap times within 107 percent. And both Mercedes and Alpine are facing fines for their respective unsafe release incidents.

Alpine’s was more minor, when “a component from the left-front wheel assembly detached and rolled through the fast lane before coming to rest in the inner lane of the pit lane.”

Meanwhile, Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli, who qualified second, left the garage with a duct cooling fan still attached, and it subsequently fell off on the track — and Lando Norris ran over it.
